vulnerability_analysis: The TeaToken contract allows the owner to set extremely high transfer fees (tax and liquidity fees up to 99% each). The owner is excluded from paying fees by default. By setting high fees and then initiating transfers from regular users, the contract accumulates a large portion of the transferred amount as fees. These fees accumulate in the contract and can be converted to liquidity, with LP tokens going to the owner. The owner can then extract value by removing liquidity or waiting for the swapAndLiquify mechanism to execute automatically.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank. 2. Set both taxFee and liquidityFee to 99 (maximum practical value). 3. Prepare a victim address with token balance. 4. Make the victim transfer tokens to another address, triggering the fee mechanism. 5. The contract will accumulate 198% of the transfer amount as fees (though capped at 100% realistically). This demonstrates the owner's ability to extract value from users.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate the owner address. 2. Call setTaxFeePercent(99) and setLiquidityFeePercent(99). 3. Create a victim address and give it some tokens. 4. Record the contract's token balance before the transfer. 5. Make the victim transfer tokens to another address. 6. Record the contract's token balance after the transfer. 7. Assert that the contract's balance increased significantly (demonstrating fee extraction).
